label: Electricity use
notes:
NOT one of the five headline ReCiPe impact categories above (those are the blended "broiler + culled breeder hen" average bird) -- this is a distinct line straight out of the same source's raw lifecycle inventory (Table 7, "2020 broiler operation lifecycle inventory flows"), which reports inputs of 0.251 kWh grid electricity plus 0.235 MJ diesel (generator) and 3.336 MJ propane heat per one broiler at 6.37 lb live weight -- the identical reference weight used throughout this block. Electricity alone is reported here because it is the metric this gap asks for; the propane and diesel heat inputs are real too but are not electricity and are left out rather than folded in.
Scope matters: this is ON-FARM GROWOUT electricity only (house ventilation, heating/cooling controls, lighting, feed/water auger motors). Hatchery incubation and processing-plant chilling, freezing and cold-chain electricity are real additional draws NOT captured in this figure and NOT currently sourced anywhere in this corpus -- the LCA's breeder-operation table (its Table 8) does report 0.0179 kWh per hatching egg for the parent/grandparent stage, but converting that into a per-broiler hatchery figure would require assumptions this source doesn't support, so it is left out rather than estimated.
No 2010 comparison is published for this line item (unlike the five ReCiPe categories above), so pct_change_decade is omitted rather than invented.

label: Fossil resource use
notes: The largest improvement of the five categories.

label: Greenhouse gas
notes: Driven down by an 8.7% feed conversion improvement and less distillers' grain in the ration. Production rose 21% while feed use rose only 11%.

label: Land use
notes: Almost entirely feed crops, not the chicken house.

label: Water consumption
notes: Dominated by feed crop irrigation. On-farm drinking and cleaning water is under 10% of the total, so "how much water does a chicken drink" is close to irrelevant to the footprint.
